question: Does profitability-sorted stock selection improve average returns while leaving substantial downside risk?
data: Kenneth French 25 portfolios formed on Size and Operating Profitability; first monthly value-weighted returns table only
definition: In each of the 5 source size quintiles compare highest, middle and lowest OP quintiles. Across-size aggregates equally weight the five corresponding source portfolios each month. No stock selection, trend filter, switching rule or future regime condition is added.
primary_descriptive_contrast: Across-size high-OP minus low-OP arithmetic mean monthly return, annualized by 12; not an alpha estimate
secondary_descriptive_measures: arithmetic mean of worst 5% of months
matched-size high-minus-low returns for all five size groups
uncertainty: Exploratory paired moving-block resampling of the same high-minus-low series; candidate blocks overlap, starts sampled independently with replacement. 12-month contiguous blocks,4000replications,seed20260930,2.5/97.5quantiles of annualized mean. No promotion test, multiple-look stopping or chosen interval.
missing_rule: Missing/nonfinite returns, duplicates or discontinuity in selected monthly sample fail; missing values never become zero.
costs: Gross research-portfolio returns, no fees, capacity, implementation or underlying annual-reconstitution cost model. Aggregation is theoretical monthly rebalancing among source portfolios; no fund or executable broker strategy is claimed.
limitations: Current revised vintage is not historical ingestion proof.
Source OP is operating profitability/book equity, not gross profits/assets or margin growth.
Negative book-equity firms and source-ineligible accounting cases are excluded by dataset construction.
Equal weights across size cells are not the market cap-weighted market.
This does not validate Prophet stock-level earnings signals, calibrated conviction, event study or risk restrictions.
No private H1/Cycle outcomes or prior refused trend-frequency experiment are read or rerun.
